summary: The entry is the observed 95% C.L. |g_aγγ| limit from a→γγ Hα non-observation in Leo T (Fig. 2 right panel, conservative Burkert curve). Particle/coupling/axes/convention match the paper, the 95% C.L. is explicitly stated (not a placeholder), representative tabulated points agree with the source curve, and the highlighted region correctly accents only this new, improving constraint.

result_identity.evidence: Fig. 2 right panel (p.4) titled '95% C.L. limits on axion-photon coupling |g_aγγ| from a→γγ ... from MUSE/VLT Hα observations of Leo T'. Extraction coupling_type AxionPhoton, g_agamma [GeV^-1] vs mass [eV], matches the right panel (not the left g_aee panel).

novelty.evidence: Paper is a new measurement (is_projection=false) presenting solid observed Hα exclusion; body (p.4) states it improves XION/CMB/HST and 'our limits lie up to two orders of magnitude below HST dwarf-galaxy bounds.' Distinct from the pre-existing blue 'Leo T' heating limit already in the compilation; reported curve is the solid observed one, not the dotted ELT/HARMONI projection.

confidence_level.evidence: Fig. 2 caption 'Figure 2. 95% C.L. limits...' and p.3 'We require the flux ... not to exceed the aperture-integrated 95% C.L. limit'. confidence_level=0.95 is paper-supported.

conventions.evidence: Eq. (S1) L ⊃ −(1/4) g_aγγ a F F̃ is the canonical convention. Axes eV / GeV^-1 match Fig. 2 right. Limit scales with Leo T DM profile (Burkert ρ0=5.4 GeV/cm^3), not local density, so dm_density/polarization null is appropriate. Plot method fills from curve up to y2 (excluded above), consistent with an upper-bound exclusion.

numerical_agreement.evidence: Vs Fig. 2 right: 497 eV→7.99e-15 matches curve bottom ~8e-15; 101.5 eV→3.35e-14; 52.8 eV→7.94e-14 track the solid Hα curve. Lyman-series dip (Ly-β, 24.18 eV)→7.99e-14 consistent with Fig. 4 and text 'up to two orders below HST (~1e-11)'. Conservative Burkert branch chosen (NFW stronger by ~1.24).

highlight_target.evidence: Highlighted PNG shows a single red region spanning ~24–500 eV from panel top down to ~8e-15, labelled 'Leo' (clipped 'Leo T Hα'), coinciding with the extracted data; the full view shows the same region correctly. No unrelated limit accented.

visibility.evidence: Region 24–500 eV, ~8e-15 to above 1e-11, fully on-screen and visible as a red band with identifying label. Narrow Lyman dips at 24–27 eV are not resolvable on the full 1e-12–1e7 eV log axis, but this is inherent to the compilation scale and the data file preserves them.
